o1.biggest_strength: It reads the data like an operator: 46-90 day buyers first, Monsoon Dark as its own problem, and subscription win-back gated behind delivery fixes.
o1.biggest_mistake: The Monsoon Dark draft does not actually name the closest replacement roast or farm, so the strongest segment still needs a better first message.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Name the exact Monsoon Dark replacement, remove the arbitrary calendar dates, use combined email/WhatsApp reachable counts where possible, and tighten the message drafts to always name a farm or roast.

o2.biggest_strength: The copy is strong, brand-safe, and the subscription section correctly leads with the delivery fix instead of a discount.
o2.biggest_mistake: It largely misses the 46-90 day at-risk group as a main target, even though they are the cheapest win-back and directly tied to the repeat-rate fall.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Put the existing 46-90 day customers first with counts, offers and value; separate them from the day-28 prevention flow; and recalc the forecast including that group and the 15% discount cases.

reason: I would rather use Output 1 because it gets the commercial order right and works from the actual segment counts. Output 2 is cleaner copy, but missing the 46-90 day group as a core win-back target is too important to overlook.
